issues.why: Stack overflow aborts the process, uncatchable (isolate.rs).
Closure stored in a variable is drawn where defined, not where called.
ignore 0.4.30 breaks MSRV 1.85 without the lockfile pin.
ignore 0.4.30 needs newer Rust than the declared MSRV.
Seal signed with --tests, checked without, reports symbols absent.
Names the default codebase name from the directory as an id-shaping ambient input.

findings.why: Args are passed without a shell; REV is the caller's own CLI argument, so option injection is possible but there is no trust boundary and no command execution.
--no-sandbox is real, but the script only parses the project's own generated diagrams (mermaid.parse); the exploit path is speculative.
Deletion is limited to orphaned files carrying the sealmap marker and is documented; the non-atomic write claim is true but minor.
Pointer and lock are written separately, but the gap is documented and verify reports it as a lock fault.
Guess is dropped when a second reachable candidate appears; it is deliberate ambiguity handling, but the doc comment's claim of stability is overstated across reachable crates.
Hash is token based and a local rename changes it; the canonicalisation promises only formatting, comment and attribute neutrality, so this is a limit rather than a bug.
Inherent-before-trait is Rust's own method resolution priority, so it is correct, not misattribution.
Macro-generated items are indeed not extracted, but this is a documented limit that the tool states openly (marked by the authors).
Pack's no-truncation guarantee covers its own text; diagram caps are documented and the full call lists stay in the index, so it is not a real contradiction.
Refusal over budget is deliberate and a shard function exists to split into packs that fit; OverBudget also reports per-seed sizes.
Refusal with --repo is real and explicit, and git archive of an absent revision errors; both are plain limitations rather than defects.
Ids depend on the --tests flag and the default codebase name.
